paragraphs.text: This whole song is twenty-nine bows, and every bow names everything as Him: fire, moon, sun, gods, things that move and things that stand still — all of it His stuff. Consciousness-shaped, many-shaped: bow.

And each bow holds two opposite things at once. Cool fire and world-devourer. Against the Veda and maker of the Veda. Sole cause of the world-round and its sole unmaker. Ever bound and ever free. Every rite and no rite at all. The word bowed with is what holds both poles together.
Near the end the litany turns: from Him to the dread ring of His powers, from merely knowing to actually embracing, from shouting victory to coming in for shelter and surrender.
